ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is a chord of the semicircle O, DE is the diameter. The tangent BC passing through point B is tangent to $\odot$O at point B, and intersects the extension line of DE at point C. Connect BD. If the quadrilateral OABC is a parallelogram, then what is the degree measure of $\angle BDC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $BC$ is the tangent of circle $O$,\\
therefore $\angle OBC=90^\circ$,\\
Since quadrilateral $ABCO$ is a parallelogram,\\
therefore $AO=BC$,\\
Also since $AO=BO$,\\
therefore $BO=BC$,\\
therefore $\angle BOC=\angle BCO=45^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BDC=\boxed{22.5^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: It can be seen from the figure: D, O, E, C are on the same straight line, and DE is the horizontal diameter; A, B are on the upper semicircular arc, the tangent BC is drawn at point B and extended to C; BD is connected, and the problem statement gives that quadrilateral OABC is a parallelogram. First use the tangent property: BC is tangent to circle O at B, so OB ⟂ BC, obtaining ∠OBC=90°. Then use the property of a parallelogram: in OABC, opposite sides are equal, so AO=BC. Also because O is the center of the circle, and A, B are both on circle O, OA=OB. Thus OB=BC. Therefore in right triangle OBC, the two legs are equal, triangle OBC is an isosceles right triangle, so ∠BOC=∠BCO=45°. Also because D, O, C are collinear, and viewed from O, OD and OC are opposite rays, ∠BOD=180°−∠BOC=135°. In triangle BOD, OB=OD (both are radii of circle O), so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal: ∠BDO=(180°−135°)/2=22.5°. Finally D, O, C are collinear, so ray DC and DO have the same direction, ∠BDC=∠BDO=22.5°.

It can be seen from the figure: D, O, E, C are on the same straight line, and DE is the horizontal diameter; A, B are on the upper semicircular arc, the tangent BC is drawn at point B and extended to C; BD is connected, and the problem statement gives that quadrilateral OABC is a parallelogram.

First use the tangent property: BC is tangent to circle O at B, so OB ⟂ BC, obtaining ∠OBC=90°.

Then use the property of a parallelogram: in OABC, opposite sides are equal, so AO=BC. Also because O is the center of the circle, and A, B are both on circle O, OA=OB. Thus OB=BC.

Therefore in right triangle OBC, the two legs are equal, triangle OBC is an isosceles right triangle, so ∠BOC=∠BCO=45°.

Also because D, O, C are collinear, and viewed from O, OD and OC are opposite rays, ∠BOD=180°−∠BOC=135°.

In triangle BOD, OB=OD (both are radii of circle O), so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal: ∠BDO=(180°−135°)/2=22.5°.

Finally D, O, C are collinear, so ray DC and DO have the same direction, ∠BDC=∠BDO=22.5°.
